body:
The bottle looked clean until it dried, when a green line appeared above the water. We had filled it after the field truck passed, at a tap on the other side of the road.

The child’s blanket was drying nearby and held the same fine dust. I left the date on the page and did not try to straighten the damaged edge. Someone else might remember the same afternoon.
title: Diary page

body:
I covered the herbs when the trial vehicle passed. By evening the leaves under the cover had curled too. The neighbor said the spray could not have crossed the fence, but her laundry had the same pale grains.

We washed the small cup twice and put it away from the others. My family asked me to put the paper away with the bills. I kept it separate because the person involved might come back for it.
title: Notebook page

body:
The feed-store driver left a sack of the new treated grain and washed his hands before accepting a cup of tea. He said the sack dust burned. The delivery slip said nothing of it.

The dog would not drink from the dish left outside. The barley I sowed from that sack came up thin and spotted, row after row.
title: Letter

body:
The workers took their boots off outside after the spraying. By morning the pale dust had still traveled inside on the dog's paws. No one in the house had gone near the sprayed rows.

The lettuce bed by the door has gone limp where the dog crossed it. I set the page beside the boots.
title: Notepad page

body: The new spray came with test strips to check orchard runoff. I kept one jar on the porch to compare with the treated rows. The lid seal failed overnight and the smell reached the next farm.
title: Sample jar lid

body:
We sprayed the lower field after the seed trial. The water path runs beside it, and the wind carried the mist across. The squash along that path has blackened leaves in a long streak.

I wrote down the day because the leaves turned afterward. I kept the page separate from the bills.
title: Notebook page

body:
The calves refused their water before the county car appeared. I poured it into a spare pail and found an oily rim when it settled. We had drawn it from the same shallow well as ours.

The child’s blanket was drying nearby and held the same fine dust. I had meant to save it only until someone could explain the difference. By then the ordinary work around us had stopped.
title: Letter

body:
The driver washed the spray rig beside the feed shop. The rinse ran down the drain toward the vegetable plots behind the houses, and by the next week the cabbages there had yellowed in a fan shape.

We washed the small cup twice and put it away from the others. I noted the cabbage rows on the page.
title: Notepad page

body:
The first rain after the field treatment left yellow flecks in a pan under the leak. The same flecks sit on the wheat leaves, thick along the rows we sprayed and absent where we did not.

The dog would not drink from the dish left outside. I saved the pan because no one believed me when I described it.
title: Diary page

body:
The seed counter receipt lists a small charge for sample jars and a sack of the new treated seed. The shopkeeper wrote a field number beside it. The corn from that sack came up grey-streaked and stunted.

I kept the receipt with my planting notes so I could compare the rows.
title: Notebook page
